title: Both of These Men Are About to Die

beats.narration: Both of these men are about to die.

claims.claim: Two men died.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees

beats.narration: Neither one will feel a thing.

claims.claim: There is no warning and it cannot be sensed.
claims.quote: The exposed person has no warning and cannot sense that the oxygen level is too low

beats.narration: What kills them has already killed eighty people at work. And you're breathing it right now.

claims.claim: They died of nitrogen asphyxiation.
claims.quote: nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: Nitrogen asphyxiation killed 80 people in US workplaces, 1992 to 2002.
claims.quote: 80 people were killed and 50 were injured

claims.claim: The period and setting of that count.
claims.quote: Nitrogen asphyxiation hazards in industry resulted in 80 deaths from 1992 to 2002

claims.claim: Nitrogen is 78 percent of the air we breathe.
claims.quote: Nitrogen, which makes up 78 percent of the air we breathe, is non-toxic

beats.narration: It's a gas called nitrogen. And they're standing on a giant steel tank that's full of it.

claims.claim: They died of nitrogen asphyxiation.
claims.quote: nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: The vessel was nitrogen-filled.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor

claims.claim: They worked on a platform at the top of the reactor.
claims.quote: Reactor R1 work platform

beats.narration: The tank is part of an oil refinery, and it has one purpose: making fuel. Inside, thick heavy oil is cooked under enormous heat and pressure, until it breaks down into gasoline and jet fuel.

claims.claim: It is a refinery unit that turns heavy oil into lighter products using high pressure and catalyst.
claims.quote: The hydrocracker unit converts heavy oil fractions to lighter molecular structure hydrocarbons using high pressure hydrogen and catalysts

claims.claim: Hydrocracking uses high pressure, high temperature and a catalyst to crack heavier feedstocks.
claims.quote: heavier feedstocks are cracked in the presence of hydrogen to produce more desirable products. The process employs high pressure, high temperature, a catalyst, and hydrogen

claims.claim: Its products include gasoline components and jet fuel.
claims.quote: Depending on the products desired (gasoline components, jet fuel, and gas oil)

claims.claim: It is a refinery.
claims.quote: refinery in Delaware City, Delaware

claims.claim: Gasoline is the most important refinery product.
claims.quote: The most important refinery product is motor gasoline

beats.narration: The tank is packed with a material that makes that happen. Sometimes that material wears out. So the tank is shut down, opened at the top, and refilled with a fresh batch.

claims.claim: The reactor holds catalyst.
claims.quote: A tray is a perforated platform installed inside a reactor used to support catalyst material

claims.claim: Catalyst gets spent and is recharged.
claims.quote: when handling spent catalyst, recharging catalyst

claims.claim: It had just been loaded with new catalyst during a shutdown.
claims.quote: finished loading the reactor with the new catalyst

claims.claim: This was a maintenance shutdown.
claims.quote: maintenance turnaround (unit shutdown)

claims.claim: The top manway was the open access point.
claims.quote: placed a temporary plastic tarp and wooden cover over the open manway

beats.narration: But the fresh batch can't touch oxygen. So the tank is pumped full of nitrogen, on purpose, and kept that way until the hatch on top is bolted shut.

claims.claim: The purge protected newly loaded catalyst from oxygen.
claims.quote: protect the newly loaded catalyst from reacting with oxygen in the air

claims.claim: Purging means pumping in nitrogen to remove oxygen.
claims.quote: Purging is the process of pumping inert gas, such as nitrogen, into pressure vessels, pipes, and other equipment to remove oxygen or other hazardous gases

claims.claim: It was a deliberate step in the procedure.
claims.quote: as part of the catalyst loading procedure

claims.claim: The nitrogen was needed until the reactor was resealed.
claims.quote: until the reactor was resealed

claims.claim: It vented out of the open top manway.
claims.quote: The nitrogen purge gas was slowly venting out of the reactor through the manway

beats.narration: Nitrogen is most of the air around you. Harmless, until it's all there is.

claims.claim: Nitrogen is 78 percent of air and non-toxic.
claims.quote: Nitrogen, which makes up 78 percent of the air we breathe, is non-toxic

claims.claim: It is safe only when mixed with enough oxygen.
claims.quote: nitrogen is safe to breathe only when mixed with the appropriate amount of oxygen

claims.claim: It is a hazard when it displaces oxygen.
claims.quote: It presents a hazard when it displaces oxygen

claims.claim: Normal air is about 21 percent oxygen.
claims.quote: The normal oxygen concentration in air is about 21 percent

beats.narration: One or two breaths of pure nitrogen and you black out. No smell. No taste. No warning.

claims.claim: Unconsciousness after one or two breaths.
claims.quote: unconsciousness after only one or two breaths

claims.claim: Odorless, tasteless, colorless.
claims.quote: nitrogen, which is odorless, tasteless, and colorless

claims.claim: No warning.
claims.quote: The exposed person has no warning and cannot sense that the oxygen level is too low

beats.narration: That's tonight's job for these two: bolt the lid back on.

claims.claim: Night-shift crew.
claims.quote: Matrix nightshift boilermaker crew

claims.claim: The job: reassemble the pipe that closes the top manway.
claims.quote: Pipe assembly connects 12-inch diameter process pipe to the reactor top manway

claims.claim: Bolting.
claims.quote: reinstalling the stud nuts and washers

claims.claim: Date.
claims.quote: November 5, 2005, nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: Place.
claims.quote: refinery in Delaware City, Delaware

beats.narration: But until that lid is on, the gas keeps leaking out of the open hole. Lean over it, and that's what you could be breathing.

claims.claim: The nitrogen was needed until the reactor was resealed.
claims.quote: until the reactor was resealed

claims.claim: It flowed out of the reactor through the open top manway.
claims.quote: The nitrogen flowed slowly out of the reactor through the

claims.claim: The purge vented straight onto the work platform.
claims.quote: the reactor was on a nitrogen purge that vented directly onto the work platform area

claims.claim: Outside, near the opening, the air could be unsafe.
claims.quote: an oxygen-depleted, hazardous atmosphere might be present outside the equipment near unsealed equipment openings

claims.claim: Above the opening he could have been breathing oxygen-deficient air.
claims.quote: the first victim could have been exposed to an oxygen-deficient atmosphere above the opening

beats.narration: And nothing warns them. No sign. No barrier. Their work permit says nitrogen: not applicable.

claims.claim: No nitrogen warning sign or barricade was in place, contrary to site procedure.
claims.quote: contrary to the Valero refinery safety procedures, a nitrogen purge warning sign and barricade were not in place in the work area

claims.claim: No warning sign was on the manway at the time.
claims.quote: no warning sign was in place at the time of the incident

claims.claim: Their permit marked the nitrogen purge N/A.
claims.quote: the nitrogen purge status was marked "N/A" on the permit even though the reactor continued to be purged with nitrogen

claims.claim: Their permit did not tell them the reactor was on nitrogen purge.
claims.quote: safe work permit did not inform them that the reactor was on nitrogen purge

beats.narration: Their training covered going inside a tank. Never the air right outside one.

claims.claim: Training covered the nitrogen hazard inside a confined space.
claims.quote: hazard awareness and confined space training that addressed the confined space nitrogen asphyxiation hazard

claims.claim: Workers told investigators their training did not cover the air outside the opening.
claims.quote: stated that their training did not address the possibility that an

claims.claim: ...outside the confined space, near the access opening.
claims.quote: atmosphere might be present outside the confined space near the access opening

claims.claim: The risk outside the space is not broadly recognised.
claims.quote: is not broadly recognized to be a hazard to workers

beats.narration: Then someone spots a roll of duct tape, five feet down inside. It has to come out.

claims.claim: A pipefitter pointed out the tape.
claims.quote: a Matrix pipefitter told them that a roll of duct tape was lying on the

claims.claim: About five feet below the opening.
claims.quote: about five feet below the opening

claims.claim: It could not be left inside.
claims.quote: reactor cleanliness criteria prohibited leaving the tape inside the reactor

beats.narration: Going inside means a permit, a special crew, and a delay. So they stay outside, bend a wire into a hook, and go fishing.

claims.claim: Entry needed a trained crew and a permit.
claims.quote: knew entry would require a specially trained and equipped crew and confined space

claims.claim: That meant a delay, possibly past the end of the shift.
claims.quote: which would delay their work, possibly beyond the end of their work shift

claims.claim: They made a wire hook instead of entering.
claims.quote: Instead, they decided to make a long wire hook

claims.claim: They knew a permit was required to enter, and discussed it.
claims.quote: knew a confined space entry safe work permit would be required if they could not retrieve the tape with the wire hook

beats.narration: He tries standing. He tries kneeling. He can't reach it.

claims.claim: Standing, then kneeling.
claims.quote: He tried from a standing position next to the manway and then, apparently to get closer, tried kneeling on the platform next to the manway

claims.claim: He could not hook it.
claims.quote: he was unable to hook the tape and remove it from the reactor

beats.narration: So, investigators believe, he sits on the edge of the hole, and puts his legs in.

claims.claim: CSB's conclusion: he likely sat on the ledge.
claims.quote: the CSB concluded that the first victim likely stepped over the manway studs and then sat on the narrow ledge

claims.claim: Legs inside.
claims.quote: sat down, and dangled his legs inside the reactor

beats.narration: The air is dead still. The gas may be sitting right around his head.

claims.claim: Calm air: the nitrogen may have collected above the opening.
claims.quote: the air was very calm, so the nitrogen purge gas may have accumulated above the manway

claims.claim: Sitting there he could have been breathing oxygen-deficient air.
claims.quote: the first victim could have been exposed to an oxygen-deficient atmosphere above the opening

claims.claim: He could have passed out without warning and slid in (one of two scenarios).
claims.quote: he could have become disoriented or lost consciousness from oxygen deprivation

beats.narration: Nobody saw what happened next.

claims.claim: Nobody saw him enter; fell or went in on purpose is unknown.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor, but he either fell in or intentionally went into the reactor

beats.narration: His foreman looks into the hole.

claims.claim: The foreman looked through the manway.
claims.quote: saw the boilermaker foreman (the second victim) and the nightshift contract administrator looking through the manway into R1

claims.claim: He most likely saw him collapse.
claims.quote: most likely saw him collapse on the tray

beats.narration: More than twenty-five years in refineries. A man who taught safety to other workers.

claims.claim: His experience and that he taught hazard awareness.
claims.quote: the second had more than 25, and had provided hazard awareness training to many co-workers throughout his career

beats.narration: Everything he's been trained to do says: stay out.
onscreen: THE MOMENT IT COULD'VE BEEN STOPPED

claims.claim: His training said stay on the platform and radio.
claims.quote: Had the foreman applied his emergency response training, he would have immediately announced the emergency on the radio and remained on the platform, safely away from the manway until qualified emergency response personnel arrived

beats.narration: Investigators suspect he thought he could hold his breath, like underwater.

claims.claim: CSB: the rescue attempt suggests workers may believe they can hold their breath.
claims.quote: suggest that some workers may believe that they can hold their breath long enough to enter an

claims.claim: The comparison with swimming underwater is the report's.
claims.quote: similarly to their ability to hold their breath when they swim underwater

beats.narration: But water makes you fight. Nitrogen feels like air. You just breathe.

claims.claim: Inhaling water makes a swimmer cough: a stimulus to resist breathing.
claims.quote: inhaling water causes sudden, uncontrollable coughing

claims.claim: That stimulus helps a swimmer hold on.
claims.quote: This is a powerful stimulus that helps a swimmer resist the body

claims.claim: Nitrogen gives no such stimulus.
claims.quote: provides no stimulus to voluntarily resist the breathing reflex

claims.claim: In an emergency a person is extremely unlikely to hold their breath.
claims.quote: it is extremely unlikely that a person would hold their breath

beats.narration: He grabs a ladder and climbs in to save him.

claims.claim: He grabbed a ladder and climbed in.
claims.quote: the foreman grabbed a nearby ladder, shoved it down the manway, and quickly climbed in the reactor

claims.claim: He was attempting a rescue.
claims.quote: His co-worker, the crew foreman, was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

claims.claim: The urge to help overwhelmed his training.
claims.quote: overwhelmed his refinery work experience, safety training, and proper emergency response protocols

beats.narration: A few breaths later, he's lying beside him.

claims.claim: He succumbed within a few breaths.
claims.quote: Within a few breaths the foreman was the second victim to succumb to oxygen deprivation

claims.claim: Both were found lying on the tray.
claims.quote: saw two victims lying motionless inside the reactor on the tray

beats.narration: Rescuers arrive in under two minutes. They lower an oxygen meter into the hole. It alarms at once: almost no oxygen.

claims.claim: Responders arrived in under two minutes.
claims.quote: arrived on the platform in less than two minutes

claims.claim: They put an oxygen meter through the manway.
claims.quote: They inserted an oxygen meter

claims.claim: It alarmed immediately: oxygen near zero.
claims.quote: through the manway and it immediately alarmed—the oxygen concentration was near zero

claims.claim: Responders used breathing apparatus.
claims.quote: A Valero operator put on his self-contained breathing air respirator then entered the reactor

beats.narration: Both men were pronounced dead.

claims.claim: Both were pronounced dead.
claims.quote: transported to the hospital where they were pronounced dead

claims.claim: They were without adequate oxygen for nearly ten minutes.
claims.quote: the two victims were deprived of adequate oxygen for nearly ten minutes

claims.claim: Recovery through the opening was very difficult.
claims.quote: recovering them from the reactor was very difficult

beats.narration: Afterwards, a warning sign went up at that hatch. The refinery's own rules had required one all along.

claims.claim: A warning sign was on the manway after the incident.
claims.quote: Confined space warning sign on the unsecured reactor manway after the incident

claims.claim: A nitrogen-purge barricade and warning were installed on the platform after the incident.
claims.quote: Nitrogen-purge controlled area barricade and warning installed on the R1 platform after the incident

claims.claim: Site procedure required a barricade and warning signs at access points...
claims.quote: The procedures required operators to install a barricade and post warning signs at all equipment access points

claims.claim: ...before the purge was started.
claims.quote: before the nitrogen purge was started

claims.claim: They were not used at this manway that night.
claims.quote: The barricade and control log were not used at the R1 manway the night of the incident

beats.narration: You don't have to climb inside a tank for it to kill you.

claims.claim: CSB: hazardous atmospheres may be present outside the space, near openings.
claims.quote: atmospheres may be present outside the confined space, near openings

claims.claim: CSB recommendation: training must say so.
claims.quote: An oxygen-deficient atmosphere might exist outside a confined space opening

claims.claim: CSB lesson: barriers and warnings round open purge vents.
claims.quote: Barriers and warnings should be maintained around open purge vents at all times during purging activities

beats.narration: If someone goes down in a tank, you do not go in after them. You call it in.
onscreen: OF CONFINED-SPACE DEATHS IN ONE STUDY

claims.claim: Only trained, equipped people should attempt a rescue.
claims.quote: Only qualified and trained personnel equipped with the necessary safety equipment should attempt a rescue

claims.claim: A third man stopped at the ladder and radioed for help (shown).
claims.quote: saw the nightshift contract administrator approach the ladder, hesitate, and then heard him urgently call for help on his radio

claims.claim: In one study 39 percent of confined-space deaths were would-be rescuers.
claims.quote: of 88 total confined space entry fatalities, 34 workers (39 percent) died while attempting to rescue a co-worker

beats.narration: Two men never came home. We tell their story so no other family goes through this.
onscreen: One died trying to save the other.

claims.claim: Two died.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees

claims.claim: Date and place.
claims.quote: November 5, 2005, nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: Their experience.
claims.quote: The first victim had nearly ten years experience working in refineries; the second had more than 25

claims.claim: The foreman died attempting to rescue the first worker.
claims.quote: was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

beats.narration: Don't die at work today.
